docs/benchmarks.md:9:This report has two independent halves: **performance** (how fast) and **output quality** (how correct/complete). They're measured differently on purpose — a fast tool that produces wrong output isn't actually useful, and this project's whole premise is "faster AND at least as accurate," so both get held to a real, reproducible standard here. Every number below has a script in `apps/validate/` or `crates/core/benches/` that reproduces it — see [Reproducing these numbers](#reproducing-these-numbers).
docs/benchmarks.md:85:"Coverage: N/M (X%)" was the only quality metric this repo had before this report — a raw prop-count ratio that didn't account for known, deliberate design differences. This section replaces it with a real per-prop agreement rate and a taxonomy of _why_ props disagree, computed by `apps/validate/src/analyze.ts` from all three tools' real output on all 21 fixture libraries.

docs/measurement.md:33:RDT has mistakes of its own. With `--oracle` the run also asks TypeScript 7.1's checker (`apps/validate/src/oracle.ts`, `typescript/sync` of `7.1.0-beta`) for each prop's type and compares it structurally with Caliper's canonical `--json`. The weekly table shows the share of props that agree (identical, or the same type spelled by name) and the share the checker contradicts. This is information only: the checker is a beta and the backend that uses it is an opt-in (`docs/type-checker-integration.md`).
docs/performance.md:44:RDT (`withCustomConfig`, `shouldExtractLiteralValuesFromEnum`, `shouldRemoveUndefinedFromOptional`) took 1.6 to 27 s and 0.6 to 2.7 GB per repo. The fixture harness also gained the switch: `CALIPER_LOAD_DEPENDENCIES=1 pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-validate run:ours`, then `parity.ts caliper-docgen`.
docs/rdt-coverage.md:3:Maps each react-docgen-typescript (RDT) output field and component pattern to the fixtures that exercise it. Run `cargo test -p caliper-docgen-core --test snapshots` to validate the original 8 snapshot fixtures. The 8 real-world library fixtures added since (fluentui, base-ui, antd, ark-ui, zendesk-garden, day-picker, headlessui, blueprint) aren't snapshot-tested — validate them via `pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-validate compare:all`.
docs/rdt-coverage.md:406:Found by a full-fixture validation sweep (`apps/validate`'s comparison across all 20 libraries at once, not a per-fixture check) — `antd/Button/Button` showed `ours found nothing` despite the component clearly being extracted correctly under a different name. antd's real `Button` export:
docs/storybook-parity.md:16:| Storybook's docgen | `@storybook/react`'s own `docgen-worker.js` (react-component-meta), unmodified, called as a middleware. It needs the TypeScript 5/6 compiler API, so `typescript` is redirected to `apps/validate`'s TypeScript 6 (`--typescript` overrides); this package's TypeScript 7 has none. |
docs/type-checker-integration.md:118:**Beta re-probe (2026-10-21, `7.1.0-beta`).** `crates/tsc-client`'s smoke example spawned the beta's `bin/tsc --api`, completed the `initialize` round trip (`caseSensitivity`, `currentDirectory`) and shut down cleanly with exit status 0, so framing and shutdown behave as the fake-tsc harness assumes. `TSC_PACKAGE_DIR=<dir> cargo run -p caliper-docgen-tsc-client --example smoke_real_tsc` repeats it against any installed `typescript`. The beta's `proto.generated.d.ts` still exposes every checker call the algorithm uses: `getTypeAtLocation`, `getTypeOfSymbol`, `getDeclaredTypeOfSymbol`, `getSignaturesOfType`, `getResolvedSignature`, `getReturnTypeOfSignature`, `getBaseTypes` and `getPropertiesOfType`. The fixture-corpus parity run below was re-run on the beta on 2026-10-23 (`apps/validate` now imports `typescript-beta`, `npm:typescript@7.1.0-beta`, since the `unstable/*` entry points are gone). Two beta behaviors to know: the server panics (`interface conversion: interface {} is string, not float64`) when `createProgram` gets string-valued enum options such as `target: 'es2022'`, so pass options from `parseConfigFile`; and `true`/`false` literal types carry neither `value` nor `intrinsicName`, so read them with `typeToString`. Discovery over a whole project ran in the oracle: 33 to 1,531 components per corpus.
docs/type-checker-integration.md:132:Method: RDT 2.4.0 on typescript@6.0.3 (`apps/validate`'s RDT is pinned to a TS6 API — see "The RDT oracle" below) with the harness options (`shouldExtractLiteralValuesFromEnum`, `shouldRemoveUndefinedFromOptional`, `propFilter: { skipPropsWithoutDoc: false }`), against the algorithm above via `apps/validate/src/run-semantic.ts` on the nightly named in each row, or `7.1.0-beta`. Run with `pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-validate parity` (`PARITY_SHOW=all` lists every mismatch).
docs/type-checker-integration.md:200:`apps/validate` depends on TypeScript 7.1 directly (for `run-semantic.ts`'s own `tsc --api` probe and the oracle), but RDT 2.4.0 crashes on import against it (`ts.JsxEmit` is undefined). RDT now resolves its `typescript` peer to `typescript@6.0.3` instead, via the aliased `typescript-beta` dependency (`npm:typescript@7.1.0-beta`, pinned exactly) the probe and oracle import from — no pnpm override needed, since pnpm overrides don't reliably rewrite a peer dependency's resolution (tried `pnpm-workspace.yaml`'s `overrides: { "react-docgen-typescript>typescript": ... }`; the lockfile recorded it but RDT kept resolving against whatever `typescript` apps/validate depended on directly).
docs/type-checker-integration.md:202:`compare.ts`/`analyze.ts` (caliper-docgen vs RDT/react-docgen) still compare only name, `required`, type and default, and render our types themselves in `run-ours.ts` (objects print as `{ ... }`). Their type mismatches mix resolver and renderer differences, and description, `parent` and `declarations` are never compared. `parity.ts` (RDT vs the semantic algorithm) compares description too.

docs/type-checker-integration.md:118:**Beta re-probe (2026-10-21, `7.1.0-beta`).** `crates/tsc-client`'s smoke example spawned the beta's `bin/tsc --api`, completed the `initialize` round trip (`caseSensitivity`, `currentDirectory`) and shut down cleanly with exit status 0, so framing and shutdown behave as the fake-tsc harness assumes. `TSC_PACKAGE_DIR=<dir> cargo run -p caliper-docgen-tsc-client --example smoke_real_tsc` repeats it against any installed `typescript`. The beta's `proto.generated.d.ts` still exposes every checker call the algorithm uses: `getTypeAtLocation`, `getTypeOfSymbol`, `getDeclaredTypeOfSymbol`, `getSignaturesOfType`, `getResolvedSignature`, `getReturnTypeOfSignature`, `getBaseTypes` and `getPropertiesOfType`. The fixture-corpus parity run below was re-run on the beta on 2026-10-23 (`apps/validate` now imports `typescript-beta`, `npm:typescript@7.1.0-beta`, since the `unstable/*` entry points are gone). Two beta behaviors to know: the server panics (`interface conversion: interface {} is string, not float64`) when `createProgram` gets string-valued enum options such as `target: 'es2022'`, so pass options from `parseConfigFile`; and `true`/`false` literal types carry neither `value` nor `intrinsicName`, so read them with `typeToString`. Discovery over a whole project ran in the oracle: 33 to 1,531 components per corpus.
docs/type-checker-integration.md:132:Method: RDT 2.4.0 on typescript@6.0.3 (`apps/validate`'s RDT is pinned to a TS6 API — see "The RDT oracle" below) with the harness options (`shouldExtractLiteralValuesFromEnum`, `shouldRemoveUndefinedFromOptional`, `propFilter: { skipPropsWithoutDoc: false }`), against the algorithm above via `apps/validate/src/run-semantic.ts` on the nightly named in each row, or `7.1.0-beta`. Run with `pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-validate parity` (`PARITY_SHOW=all` lists every mismatch).
docs/type-checker-integration.md:200:`apps/validate` depends on TypeScript 7.1 directly (for `run-semantic.ts`'s own `tsc --api` probe and the oracle), but RDT 2.4.0 crashes on import against it (`ts.JsxEmit` is undefined). RDT now resolves its `typescript` peer to `typescript@6.0.3` instead, via the aliased `typescript-beta` dependency (`npm:typescript@7.1.0-beta`, pinned exactly) the probe and oracle import from — no pnpm override needed, since pnpm overrides don't reliably rewrite a peer dependency's resolution (tried `pnpm-workspace.yaml`'s `overrides: { "react-docgen-typescript>typescript": ... }`; the lockfile recorded it but RDT kept resolving against whatever `typescript` apps/validate depended on directly).
docs/type-checker-integration.md:202:`compare.ts`/`analyze.ts` (caliper-docgen vs RDT/react-docgen) still compare only name, `required`, type and default, and render our types themselves in `run-ours.ts` (objects print as `{ ... }`). Their type mismatches mix resolver and renderer differences, and description, `parent` and `declarations` are never compared. `parity.ts` (RDT vs the semantic algorithm) compares description too.

content.content:
language: typescript

tasks:
  compare:
    command: pnpm compare:all
    deps:
      - "cli:build"
    inputs:
      - "src/**/*"
    options:
      cache: false
baselines/
node_modules/
analysis.json
bench-cold*.json
bench-cold*.md
# https://moonrepo.dev/docs/config/workspace
$schema: "https://moonrepo.dev/schemas/workspace.json"

projects:
  core: "crates/core"
  cli: "crates/cli"
  cli-npm: "packages/cli"
  crates-binding: "crates/binding"
  napi: "packages/napi"
  validate: "apps/validate"
  vite-plugin: "packages/vite-plugin"
  storybook: "packages/storybook"

vcs:
  client: git
  defaultBranch: main
  sync: true
  hooks:
    pre-commit:
      - '. "$HOME/.cargo/env"'
      # Defined in the justfile so the hook and `just ci` share one definition.
      # Re-run `moon sync vcs-hooks` after changing this list.
      - "just pre-commit"

telemetry: false
test-rust:
    cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude caliper-docgen-napi --locked
    cargo test --doc --workspace --exclude caliper-docgen-napi

# Run TypeScript tests
test-ts:
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-vite-plugin test
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-storybook test
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-validate test

# Build the native binding and run the Vite plugin against it
test-integration:
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-napi build:napi
    NAPI_BINARY_REQUIRED=true pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-vite-plugin test:integration
    NAPI_BINARY_REQUIRED=true pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-storybook test:integration

    cargo deny check

# Everything the CI jobs run, minus the Node version matrix and verify-install
ci: lint test deny typos zizmor doc-check machete semver msrv (coverage "90")

# Run moon compare task (accuracy vs react-docgen + react-docgen-typescript)
compare:
    moon run validate:compare

# Time and memory of this checkout (or a branch) against origin/main on Mantine and Chakra; see docs/measurement.md.
bench *args:
    python3 scripts/bench.py {{args}}

# Clean build artifacts
clean:
    moon clean
  "overrides": [
    {
      "files": ["**/tests/**/*.ts", "**/*.test.ts"],
      "plugins": ["typescript", "unicorn", "oxc", "vitest"]
    },
    {
      "files": ["apps/validate/src/**/*.ts", "packages/cli/bin/cli.js"],
      "rules": {
        "node/no-sync": "off"
      }
    }
  ],
  "env": {
    "builtin": true
  }
}
[files]
extend-exclude = ["apps/validate/baselines/"]

[default.extend-words]
# variable abbreviations used in pattern bindings
afe = "afe"
sme = "sme"
# ratatui is a real Rust TUI library
ratatui = "ratatui"
# beng is a real Unicode CLDR numbering-system identifier (Bengali)
beng = "beng"
# onSeeked is React's media event handler
Seeked = "Seeked"
packages:
  - "packages/*"
  - "apps/*"
allowBuilds:
  esbuild: true

# packages/cli and packages/napi declare optionalDependencies on their own
# per-platform artifact packages, which the release pipeline publishes. None of
# them exist on the registry yet, so a clean `--frozen-lockfile` install -- what
# CI always does -- compared those specifiers against a lockfile that cannot
# record them and failed. Consumers installing from npm are unaffected: this
# only governs this workspace's own install.
ignoredOptionalDependencies:
  - "caliper-docgen-*"
  - "caliper-docgen-napi-*"

For each corpus it records, per tool, the wall time and peak RSS of one whole run (process start included), and for
Caliper the canonical JSON's size. Recall is measured against RDT: of the components RDT reports with props, how many
the tool also reports (same file, same name), and of their props, how many it lists, split into the props `@types/react`
declares and the rest. react-docgen reads each file alone, so it lists none of React's. With --oracle it also records
how often TypeScript 7.1's checker contradicts Caliper's prop types. That is information, never a gate.

--previous FILE compares with an earlier record (the last green run's artifact) and, when Caliper is more than 10%
slower or uses more than 10% more memory, or its recall falls by more than 2 points, writes --issue FILE for the
workflow to open or update one issue with. Nothing here fails a pull request.

Usage: scripts/weekly.py --bin BIN [--corpus NAME]... [--corpora DIR] [--work DIR] [--runs N] [--oracle]
                         [--previous FILE] [--out FILE] [--markdown FILE] [--issue FILE]

content.content:
# Benchmarks: caliper-docgen vs. react-docgen-typescript vs. react-docgen

**Generated:** 2026-07-25.

**Hardware:** Apple Silicon (arm64), macOS. Numbers below are absolute and will shift on different hardware — treat the _relative_ comparisons as the durable signal, not the absolute milliseconds.

Whole-library numbers on five pinned public corpora, and the CI gates that hold them, are in [`performance.md`](performance.md). The output-quality half of this report is a 2026-07-25 snapshot on the fixture libraries; current agreement with RDT on installed repos is in [`parity.md`](parity.md).

This report has two independent halves: **performance** (how fast) and **output quality** (how correct/complete). They're measured differently on purpose — a fast tool that produces wrong output isn't actually useful, and this project's whole premise is "faster AND at least as accurate," so both get held to a real, reproducible standard here. Every number below has a script in `apps/validate/` or `crates/core/benches/` that reproduces it — see [Reproducing these numbers](#reproducing-these-numbers).

## Tools compared

| Tool                      | Version   | Approach                                         |
| ------------------------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `caliper-docgen`          | this repo | OXC parser, no type-checking pass                |
| `react-docgen-typescript` | 2.2.2     | full `ts.Program` + real TypeScript type checker |
----

---

## Output quality

"Coverage: N/M (X%)" was the only quality metric this repo had before this report — a raw prop-count ratio that didn't account for known, deliberate design differences. This section replaces it with a real per-prop agreement rate and a taxonomy of _why_ props disagree, computed by `apps/validate/src/analyze.ts` from all three tools' real output on all 21 fixture libraries.

**Methodology note — how each tool's type string is read:**

- `react-docgen-typescript` represents union/literal prop types as `{ name: 'enum', value: [...] }` — the real type string comes from `.value`, not `.name` (literally the string `"enum"`).
- `react-docgen` puts real TypeScript type info under `.tsType` (with a `.raw` field carrying the exact source text), not `.type` (a legacy PropTypes-only field absent for TS-typed props).
----
- **Generic type-parameter substitution through multi-level type-alias chains.** Root-caused here for the `ariakit`/`ark-ui` outliers above: Ariakit's own `Props<T, O> = O & Omit<ComponentPropsWithoutRef<T>, keyof O>` pattern requires substituting a generic param (`T = "button"`) through a nested `Omit`+`ComponentPropsWithoutRef` chain — exactly the "generic parameter substitution" item already listed as Corsa-deferred. This report adds concrete evidence (4+ real-world outlier components in one corpus) that this isn't a theoretical gap.
- **`@emotion/styled`'s two-arg `styled(tag, options)<T>(fn)` overload** (`storybook-emotion/Button` — already `docs/rdt-coverage.md`'s open gap #2). RDT needs a type checker for this too — not a competitive gap.
- **`styled.X.attrs<T>()` component detection** (`zendesk-garden` — already gap #1). Shared blind spot with RDT.
- **Same-namespace sibling reference resolution** for select `@types/react` internals (`EventHandler`, `TrustedHTML` — already gap #3; visible in the 30 `UNRESOLVABLE_IMPORT` diagnostics above).

---

## Reproducing these numbers

```bash
# Performance
cargo bench -p caliper-docgen-core                    # per-fixture cold + incremental, criterion
cd apps/validate && ./bench-cold.sh                     # cross-tool cold, hyperfine (needs `brew install hyperfine`)

# Quality
cd apps/validate
pnpm run baseline                                        # generates baselines/*.json for all three tools
pnpm run analyze                                          # agreement rate + taxonomy → analysis.json
```

`analyze.ts`'s full structured output (every individual prop-level diff, not just the aggregate tables above) is written to `apps/validate/analysis.json` — useful for finding the next outlier component to investigate, not committed here since it's regenerated by the commands above.

32:### Cold extraction, all three tools under equal footing
56:### Per-fixture cold extraction (Rust-internal, criterion)
69:### Incremental single-file update — the number RDT and react-docgen cannot produce at all
83:## Output quality
100:### Agreement rate vs. react-docgen-typescript
142:### Agreement rate vs. react-docgen
174:## What this tool can provide that they can't
187:## Shortcomings and remediation plan

# Contributing

By participating in this project, you agree to abide by the [Code of Conduct](./CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). Found a security issue? See [SECURITY.md](./SECURITY.md) instead of opening a public issue.

## Prerequisites

| Tool  | Min version | Notes                                         |
| ----- | ----------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| Rust  | 1.97        | `rustup update stable`                        |
| proto | latest      | manages Node/pnpm versions from `.prototools` |
| pnpm  | 9           | via proto, or `npm i -g pnpm`                 |

After installing proto, run `moon setup` once to pull the pinned Node version and any other tool versions declared in `.prototools`.

## Build & test

```bash
# Rust
cargo build                                            # dev build
cargo test -p caliper-docgen-core                   # unit + snapshot tests
cargo clippy -p caliper-docgen-core -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --all

# TypeScript
pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-vite-plugin test      # 33 unit tests (mocked NAPI)
pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-vite-plugin test:integration  # 3 integration tests (real native binding)

# Accuracy comparison (informational — exits 0 regardless of gaps)
moon run validate:compare
```

The pre-commit hook runs `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings`, `typos`, and `cargo deny` on every commit. It's fast enough that skipping it isn't worth the trouble.

## Snapshot tests

Snapshot tests use [insta](https://insta.rs). Each fixture (shadcn, MUI, Chakra, etc.) has a snapshot of the full extraction output. If your change touches extraction output, insta will flag it:

```bash
cargo test -p caliper-docgen-core    # fails with "snapshot mismatch"
cargo insta review                     # review diffs, accept or reject
```

Accept any snapshot change that is intentional (i.e., the output got more accurate). Reject regressions.

## Where code goes

**`crates/core`** — everything that understands TypeScript ASTs and React component patterns. No I/O, no async, no terminal output. Every function here must be `Send + Sync` so rayon can parallelize it.

**`crates/cli`** — user-facing output only. No extraction logic. Commands parse args and delegate to `core::pipeline`. Error formatting uses `miette`; progress uses `indicatif`; table output uses `comfy-table`.

**`crates/binding`** — thin NAPI wrapper. Owns the async runtime (tokio) and exposes the five NAPI functions (`extractAll`, `createSession`, `initializeSession`, `extractFileIncremental`, `closeSession`). No business logic.

**`packages/napi`** — `caliper-docgen-napi`. TypeScript types (`index.d.ts`) and the dev binary loader (`index.js`) that finds the `.node` file from `target/` or `NAPI_RS_NATIVE_LIBRARY_PATH`. No logic.

**`packages/vite-plugin`** — `caliper-docgen-vite-plugin`. Single Vite `Plugin` object. No extraction logic — calls NAPI and manages HMR.

## Code style

The authoritative reference is `.claude/skills/rust-style/SKILL.md`. Highlights:

**Maps:** `FxHashMap` for internal maps (hot path, no DoS surface). `BTreeMap` for anything that ends up in JSON output (key ordering must be deterministic and stable across runs).

**Strings:** `CompactString` for type names and prop names. Most are ≤24 bytes (`string`, `boolean`, `ReactNode`, `MouseEvent`) and fit inline without heap allocation.

**Control flow:** `let...else` keeps the happy path flat:

```rust
let Some(entry) = map.get(key) else { return None };
```

**Matching on project-local enums:** no wildcards. `match status { Ok => .., Err => .. }` gives a compile error when new variants are added. `match status { Ok => .., _ => .. }` silently ignores them.

**No `unwrap()` outside tests.** Use `?` or emit a `Diagnostic` and return a safe default. The `Diagnostic` type has constructors for common error shapes.

**Comments:** only when the WHY is non-obvious. Not what the code does.

## Commits

- GPG-signed, `Signed-off-by` trailer (both configured in `.git/config`)
- `feat:` / `fix:` / `refactor:` / `chore:` / `docs:` prefix
- No line wrapping at any column
- Subject line says it all — skip the body if it adds nothing

```
# good
feat: resolve ComponentPropsWithoutRef in intersection type aliases

# bad
Updated the resolver to also handle the case where ComponentPropsWithoutRef
appears inside an intersection type alias, which was causing it to be
treated as opaque when it should expand the HTML attributes.
```

## Pull requests

1. Branch from `main`
2. Keep the pre-commit hook passing
3. Update snapshots if extraction output changes (`cargo insta review`)
4. One logical change per PR — squash fixup commits before merging

> `moon run validate:compare` is a developer tool for checking accuracy against real libraries. It exits 0 regardless of coverage gaps and is not a CI gate.

**Strings:** `CompactString` for type names and prop names. Most are ≤24 bytes (`string`, `boolean`, `ReactNode`, `MouseEvent`) and fit inline without heap allocation.

**Control flow:** `let...else` keeps the happy path flat:

```rust
let Some(entry) = map.get(key) else { return None };
```

**Matching on project-local enums:** no wildcards. `match status { Ok => .., Err => .. }` gives a compile error when new variants are added. `match status { Ok => .., _ => .. }` silently ignores them.

**No `unwrap()` outside tests.** Use `?` or emit a `Diagnostic` and return a safe default. The `Diagnostic` type has constructors for common error shapes.

**Comments:** only when the WHY is non-obvious. Not what the code does.

## Commits

- GPG-signed, `Signed-off-by` trailer (both configured in `.git/config`)
- `feat:` / `fix:` / `refactor:` / `chore:` / `docs:` prefix
- No line wrapping at any column
- Subject line says it all — skip the body if it adds nothing

```
# good
feat: resolve ComponentPropsWithoutRef in intersection type aliases

# bad
Updated the resolver to also handle the case where ComponentPropsWithoutRef
appears inside an intersection type alias, which was causing it to be
treated as opaque when it should expand the HTML attributes.
```

## Pull requests

1. Branch from `main`
2. Keep the pre-commit hook passing
3. Update snapshots if extraction output changes (`cargo insta review`)
4. One logical change per PR — squash fixup commits before merging

> `moon run validate:compare` is a developer tool for checking accuracy against real libraries. It exits 0 regardless of coverage gaps and is not a CI gate.

# Migrating from react-docgen-typescript

`caliper-docgen` targets output-shape compatibility with `react-docgen-typescript` (RDT) via the CLI's `--format rdt` flag. The NAPI binding and Vite plugin currently only expose this tool's own canonical format (`kind`-tagged `PropType`, shown in the main README) — no RDT-shape option at that layer yet.

This document covers what's compatible today, what's intentionally different, and what's a known gap rather than a design choice.

## Should you switch today?

Output should match closely if your components use:

- Plain interfaces or type aliases
- `forwardRef` (including wrapped in an `as` cast), `FC`, or HOC wrapping
- `Omit` / `Pick`
- `VariantProps` (CVA / TV / PandaCSS)
- Discriminated unions (including ones wrapped in an intersection)

Scraping the full 250+ inherited HTML attributes per component? It's supported, but opt-in — see [HTML attribute inheritance](#html-attribute-inheritance) below.

## Field-by-field comparison

### Component level (`ComponentDoc`)

| RDT field | `--format rdt` | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `displayName` | ✅ |  |
| `description` | ✅ | From the component's own leading JSDoc, if any |
| `props` | ✅ | See prop-level table below |
| `methods` | ✅ (always `[]`) | RDT only populates this for class components; we don't support class components, so it's always empty — present for shape compatibility, not because we detect methods |
| `tags` | ✅ | JSDoc `@tag` values on the component declaration (e.g. `@deprecated`, `@since`) — not part of RDT's original spec but included since some tooling reads it |

### Prop level (`PropItem`)

| RDT field | `--format rdt` | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | ✅ |  |
| `required` | ✅ |  |
| `type.name` | ✅ | Literal unions emit `{name: "enum", value: [...]}` matching RDT's convention (so Storybook-style `<select>` controls activate) instead of inlining the literal text |
| `description` | ✅ |  |
| `defaultValue` | ✅ | `{value, computed}` — captured from destructured parameter defaults (`{ variant = 'primary' }`) or JSDoc `@default`, code value wins on conflict |
| `parent.name` / `parent.fileName` | ✅ | `fileName` is always canonicalized to an absolute path regardless of how `--src` was invoked |
| `props.children` | ✅ | Omitted when it has no description, matching RDT's default `skipChildrenPropWithoutDoc`; `--format canonical` keeps it |
| `declarations` | ❌ not emitted in `--format rdt` | Only present in `--format canonical` (the raw internal shape); omitted from `--format rdt` to match RDT's single-parent shape. File an issue if you need it |

### Intentionally omitted

| Prop | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `ref` | Not a user-facing prop — a React internal. RDT includes it because it walks the full inherited type; we treat it as noise |
| `key` | Same reasoning as `ref` |

### HTML attribute inheritance

RDT inlines every inherited HTML attribute (e.g. all ~250-300 members of `ButtonHTMLAttributes`) directly into `props`. This tool doesn't, by default — set `--html-attributes` to control it:

| Mode | Behavior | Reaches `--format rdt` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `curated` | A compact subset per element (handlers, `aria-*`, `ref`, common attributes, the element's notable ones) in `notableInherited`. `inheritance` (canonical format only) still records the full layer — element, `Omit`-ted keys. | No |
| `full` (default) | Resolves `@types/react`'s real `HTMLAttributes`/`AriaAttributes`/`DOMAttributes`/`<Element>HTMLAttributes` chain and merges it directly into `props`, matching RDT's flat behavior. | Yes |
| `none` | Own-declared props only. | Yes (nothing to add) |

Flag by layer: `--html-attributes full` (CLI), `htmlAttributes: 'full'` (NAPI), `htmlAttributes: "full"` (`docgen.config.ts`).

**`full` mode accuracy:** verified against a real button, 238 of ~250 real attributes resolve. The remainder is a narrow gap — a handful of `@types/react` fields reference a same-namespace sibling type without an explicit qualifier, which degrades to an `UNRESOLVABLE_IMPORT` diagnostic on that one field rather than a crash or missing component. Details in `docs/rdt-coverage.md`'s "HtmlAttributeMode" section.

If you need the full attribute set and aren't ready to opt into `full` mode, this is the main compatibility gap to check for your specific components.

## Getting the exact diff for your codebase

`apps/validate/` is the harness used to compare this tool's output against a real `react-docgen-typescript` run, field by field, across 20 real component libraries (shadcn, MUI, Chakra, Mantine, React Aria, Radix, Fluent UI, Base UI, Ant Design, Ark UI, Zendesk Garden, React Day Picker, Headless UI, Blueprint, and others — full list in `docs/rdt-coverage.md`).

Don't just trust this document — run it against your own components:

```bash
pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-validate compare:all
```

`docs/rdt-coverage.md` tracks which pattern each fixture exercises and the bugs found along the way (almost all now fixed).
